content.Title: Meet Aiphin: one team, every expert
content.Objective: Introduce the agency and the mascot. In one reel the viewer learns the name (AY-fin), the positioning 'One team. Every expert.' and the four services we lead with: custom CRM, AI implementation and integration, smart websites, social content.
content.Hook EN (on screen, first 1.5 s): Hi, I'm Aiphin. Your AI teammate.
content.Hook AR: مرحبًا، أنا أيفِن. زميلك في الذكاء الاصطناعي.
content.Scene plan (beat by beat):
0–2 s  Aiphin waves on the Ocean glow background, hook pops in.
2–6 s  'Most agencies sell the advice or the build. We do both.'
6–18 s  Four quick cards, one per service, each with one concrete line: Custom CRM ('built around how you sell'), AI integration ('the WhatsApp answered at 9pm'), Smart website ('answers questions at 2am'), Social content ('one voice all month, AR + EN').
18–22 s  Contrast line: 'We don't sell you a roadmap. We build it and run it.'
22–25 s  End card: stacked lockup, aiphin.me.
Visuals: Aiphin waving (new pose), Aiphin pointing at the service cards (new pose). Voice-over in the cloned Aiphin voice.
content.Caption:
Most agencies sell you either the advice or the build. A roadmap nobody implements and a system nobody planned fail the same way.

We're Aiphin: one team for custom CRMs, AI integrations, smart websites and social content. We build what we recommend, and we stay to run it.

Tell us what's slowing you down.

content.Title: 5 signs you've outgrown your CRM
content.Objective: Make distributors, project and tender businesses recognise that an off-the-shelf CRM or a spreadsheet is forcing them to change how they sell, and that a custom CRM fits the pipeline instead.
content.Hook EN (on screen, first 1.5 s): Your CRM shouldn't change how you sell.
content.Hook AR: نظام الـ CRM لا يجب أن يغيّر طريقة بيعك.
content.Scene plan (beat by beat):
S1 Hook on Night background, Aiphin thinking pose.
S2 Sign 1: sales lives in a spreadsheet the CRM never sees.
S3 Sign 2: quotes and approvals happen in WhatsApp, not in the system.
S4 Sign 3: you pay for 40 features and use 4.
S5 Sign 4: nobody trusts the pipeline numbers on Monday.
S6 Sign 5: every new step means a workaround.
S7 The fix: a CRM built around your pipeline (pipelines, quotes and approvals, roles and audit trail, WhatsApp and email threading, migration from spreadsheets or HubSpot). CTA.
Visuals: one generic CRM pipeline mockup (no real client data), Aiphin thinking.
content.Caption:
Distributors, projects, tenders, service contracts: some pipelines are genuinely different. When the tool doesn't fit, people stop using it, and the real pipeline goes back to Excel and WhatsApp.

We build CRMs around how you already sell: your stages, your quotes and approvals, your WhatsApp threads, with your spreadsheets or HubSpot data moved over.

How many of the five do you recognise?

content.Title: Leads at 9pm. Replies at 9:01pm.
content.Objective: Show the before/after of an AI assistant on WhatsApp: the lead that used to wait until 11am now gets an answer in a minute, and a human takes over with the full context.
content.Hook EN (on screen, first 1.5 s): Lead at 9pm. Reply at 11am. Too late.
content.Hook AR: عميل في التاسعة مساءً. ردّ في الحادية عشرة صباحًا. متأخر جدًا.
content.Scene plan (beat by beat):
0–3 s  BEFORE: phone at night, message arrives 21:04, clock spins to 11:00, the customer replies 'Already booked elsewhere'.
3–5 s  Split wipe to AFTER.
5–13 s  Same message at 21:04, the assistant replies at 21:05 with price range and two questions, books a call.
13–17 s  Next morning: the sales rep opens the thread with the full context ('human handoff with full context').
17–20 s  '24/7 on chat, WhatsApp, email and voice.' End card.
Visuals: animated generic chat UI built in HTML (no real app logos), Aiphin holding a smartphone (new pose) for the end card.
content.Caption:
Leads arrive at 9pm and get a reply at 11am the next day, by which time they've booked elsewhere.

We connect an AI assistant to your WhatsApp, web chat and Instagram. It answers the routine questions in a minute, qualifies the lead, and hands your team the conversation with full context in the morning.

Leads at 9pm. Replies at 9:01pm.

content.Title: Nobody wakes up wanting AI
content.Objective: A shareable point-of-view card that sets the tone: we lead with the business problem, not the technology. Builds trust with owners tired of AI hype.
content.Hook AR: لا أحد يستيقظ صباحًا وهو يريد ذكاءً اصطناعيًا.
content.Scene plan (beat by beat):
Night background, headline in Audiowide, Glow on the word 'AI' only.
Support line: 'They want the WhatsApp answered, the quote out before lunch, and the stock number to be right.'
Small Aiphin, calm pose, bottom corner facing the text. Footer aiphin.me.
Visuals: Aiphin calm smile on dark background with cyan halo (new pose).
content.Caption:
Nobody wakes up wanting AI. They want the WhatsApp answered, the quote out before lunch, and the stock number to be right.

That's where we start: with the problem. AI is only the means. And if automation isn't the answer, we say so.
content.CTA: Tell us what's slowing you down · aiphin.me

content.Title: What your website does at 2am
content.Objective: Explain the difference between a brochure website and a smart one: a site that answers, captures and tracks while the team sleeps, in Arabic and English.
content.Hook AR: الساعة الثانية فجرًا. هل موقعك يعمل؟
content.Scene plan (beat by beat):
S1 Hook, night city skyline with a glowing laptop.
S2 02:00 a visitor asks a question: the built-in assistant answers.
S3 02:03 the visitor leaves a number: lead captured and sent to the CRM.
S4 02:05 switches to Arabic: the site is RTL-ready, same experience.
S5 09:00 the team sees where the lead came from (analytics and conversion tracking).
S6 'A website that ranks and answers questions at 2am.' CTA.
Visuals: night skyline scene with laptop (new image), generic website mockup EN + AR built in HTML.
content.Caption:
Most websites are brochures: they look nice and wait. A smart website keeps working after you close.

We build fast sites with the assistant and the tracking built into the page, not bolted on: answers at 2am, leads straight into your CRM, Arabic and English from day one.

content.Title: Someone's Thursday, every Thursday
content.Objective: Dramatise the manual weekly report and show the integrated version: sources joined, numbers agreed, a digest that arrives by itself on Monday morning.
content.Hook EN (on screen, first 1.5 s): Every Thursday, someone rebuilds this report.
content.Hook AR: كل خميس، يعيد أحدهم بناء هذا التقرير من الصفر.
content.Scene plan (beat by beat):
0–6 s  Calendar flips Thursday after Thursday; the same Excel file is copied from CRM, ERP and finance by hand (copy-paste animation, three windows).
6–8 s  'Most companies don't have a software problem. They have a handover problem.'
8–16 s  The three sources connect with glowing lines into one dashboard; an automated weekly digest lands in the inbox on Monday 8:00.
16–20 s  '12 systems connected into one source of truth.' End card.
Visuals: animated HTML windows and dashboard (no real data), Aiphin looking at a holographic chart going up (new pose).
content.Caption:
Reporting is someone's Thursday, every Thursday, rebuilt from scratch in Excel.

We join the sources, agree the definitions once, and put the numbers where people check on Monday morning. The person stops being the copy-paste middle and goes back to the work they were hired for.
content.CTA: Tell us what's slowing you down · aiphin.me

content.Title: How we work: diagnose before we quote
content.Objective: Lower the risk of the first step. Show the four-step method and that the client keeps the written diagnostic whatever they decide, with one live workflow in about six weeks.
content.Hook EN (on screen, first 1.5 s): We don't quote before we diagnose.
content.Hook AR: لا نقدّم عرض سعر قبل أن نشخّص المشكلة.
content.Scene plan (beat by beat):
S1 Hook + Aiphin pointing.
S2 Diagnose: we sit with the work, count the steps, tools and waiting.
S3 Quantify: a monthly cost on each bottleneck, so numbers set the priorities.
S4 Design: the smallest fix (an integration, a bot, or deleting a step).
S5 Prove: one real workflow live before a bigger programme. '6 weeks, typical time from diagnosis to first live workflow.'
S6 'The written diagnostic is yours to keep, whatever you decide.' CTA.
Visuals: Aiphin pointing to the side (new pose); step icons built in HTML.
content.Caption:
Before we build anything, we sit with your team and find where money and hours leak. You get a written diagnosis with a ranked, costed list, not a sales deck. It's yours to keep, whatever you decide.

Then we ship one real workflow live, so you judge output, not a Gantt chart.
content.CTA: Start with a business diagnostic · aiphin.me

content.Title: We built our own product first: Stacko
content.Objective: Prove 'we build what we recommend' with something real: Stacko, the AI stock-management product Aiphin built. Shows build capability (CRM-style app, Telegram/WhatsApp-first input, live dashboards) without inventing client results.
content.Hook EN (on screen, first 1.5 s): An agency that builds its own products.
content.Scene plan (beat by beat):
0–3 s  Hook over Aiphin on Night background.
3–8 s  'The stock number should be right. So we built Stacko.' Stacko logo appears (Stacko brand assets).
8–18 s  Quick cuts of real Stacko screens inside a phone and a laptop frame: message in, stock updates, live warehouse map.
18–22 s  'The same team builds your CRM, your integrations and your website.'
22–25 s  End card: 'Stacko, a product by AIPHIN' then the Aiphin lockup + WhatsApp.
Visuals: existing Stacko screenshots from the visual library (UI frames), Aiphin typing on a holographic screen (new pose).
content.Caption:
We say we build what we recommend. Here's the proof: Stacko, the stock-management product our team designed, built and runs.

Same people, same method, for your CRM, your integrations and your website.
content.Verify before approving: Confirm the owner is happy to name Stacko publicly on Aiphin's page, and which Stacko screenshots are cleared for use.

content.Title: The copy-paste middle
content.Objective: Name the hidden cost of disconnected tools: one person retyping orders, quotes and invoices between systems. Position integration as removing that person from the middle, not replacing them.
content.Hook EN (on screen, first 1.5 s): There's a person between your systems.
content.Scene plan (beat by beat):
S1 Hook: illustration of a person between three screens (CRM, ERP, finance).
S2 'Sales lives in spreadsheets, delivery lives in the ERP, and neither trusts the other's numbers.'
S3 What they retype: the order, the quote, the invoice, the status update.
S4 What it costs: hours each week and errors nobody sees until the month closes.
S5 The fix: CRM, ERP and finance in sync; quote, invoice and approval flows; '4.2 hrs saved per employee each week.'
S6 'Take the person out of the copy-paste middle.' CTA.
Visuals: one scene image of an office worker between three monitors (new image prompt), integration diagram built in HTML.
content.Caption:
Most companies don't have a software problem. They have a handover problem.

Somewhere in your team there's a person whose real job is copying data from one system into another. We connect the systems so that person can go back to the work only a person can do.
content.CTA: Tell us what's slowing you down · aiphin.me

content.Title: Who makes this content?
content.Objective: Sell the social content service with a behind-the-scenes look at our own content system: idea, script, design, approval, publish, in Arabic and English, one voice all month.
content.Hook EN (on screen, first 1.5 s): This reel went through 5 steps before you saw it.
content.Hook AR: هذا الفيديو مرّ بخمس مراحل قبل أن يصلك.
content.Scene plan (beat by beat):
0–2 s  Hook.
2–18 s  Five quick steps on a board, each card flipping to the next: Idea (from the monthly plan) → Script (EN + AR, written natively) → Design (carousels and reels in brand) → Approval (the client approves every piece) → Publish (scheduled, then a performance review).
18–22 s  'Deciding what's worth posting is the hard part. We do that part too.'
22–25 s  End card.
Visuals: generic content board / pipeline UI built in HTML (no client names), Aiphin celebrating (new pose).
content.Caption:
Posting isn't the hard part. Deciding what's worth posting is.

We run your calendar end to end: a monthly plan by topic, carousels, reel scripts and captions written natively in Arabic and English, your approval on every piece, then a review of what worked. One voice, all month.
content.Verify before approving: Decide whether we can show our own CRM pipeline screens on camera, or only a generic mock.

40+ automation and platform projects delivered.
4.2 hours saved per employee each week.
68% of routine tickets answered without a human.
6 weeks, typically, from diagnosis to first live workflow.

One team: strategy, build and support under one contract.

content.Title: Tell us what's slowing you down
content.Objective: Direct-response close of the series. Aiphin asks the viewer three quick questions and invites them to send the answer on WhatsApp; a senior consultant replies within one business day.
content.Scene plan (beat by beat):
0–2 s  Aiphin to camera, hook.
2–14 s  Three questions pop in one by one: 'What do you answer by hand fifty times a week?' · 'Which report eats someone's whole day?' · 'Where do leads wait the longest?'
14–18 s  'Send us your answer. A senior consultant replies within one business day.'
18–20 s  End card with aiphin.me large.
Visuals: Aiphin giving a thumbs up and winking (new pose), Aiphin thinking (reuse from AIP-02).
content.Caption:
Three questions:
1. What do you answer by hand fifty times a week?
2. Which report eats someone's whole day?
3. Where do leads wait the longest?

Send us your answers in a message. A senior consultant replies within one business day, usually with two or three questions before any quote.
